title: Frontend: Progress Bar II
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Progress Bar II. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Add task[data-action=add] creates sequential IDs; at most two run. Advance[data-action=advance] adds 50 to each running task, completing at 100 before queued tasks start at zero. li[data-task=ID] text is state:progress; states queued/running/completed. This is an injected work-progress model.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Model each task as queued, running, completed, failed, or cancelled.
alternativeApproaches: Replace simulated time with real byte/work acknowledgements and keep retry progress semantics explicit.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Capacity limit; completion frees slot; cancellation.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
